brief: Tonight is Legs A, and it is your sixth training day in a row — no day off since July 19. Train it, then take Sunday July 26 completely off. That rest day is part of the plan, not a slip. Two lifts go up tonight and two get held back on purpose. Leg curls move from 120 to 135, because you already curled 135 for four straight sets on Wednesday and this day has quietly been asking you for less than you can do. Leg extensions top out at 150 for 12 — you held 142.5 for 14 twice on Wednesday, and that is what earns the next pin. The leg press stays exactly where it was on your last Legs A: 220 for the third set and 200 for the fourth. Last time you tried to hold 220 and had to come down, and adding to your heaviest lift on your sixth straight day is how you buy an injury instead of a quad. Calves are two hard sets at 260 instead of four — on a day like this you trim the end of the session, and both times you have run this day you stopped at two sets anyway. Hip adductor moves one notch to 97.5, and cable crunches go to 55 after three sets of 15 at 50. Everything else is unchanged. If anything feels sharp rather than tired, stop the set. Keep conditioning easy today — a walk if anything, and save the elliptical for after your rest day. One more thing: I read your note that the lat pulldown machine doubles as the cable row. I have not changed the program for it, because I am not allowed to edit your plan on my own — bring it up in a Claude session and we will fix how that slot is written.

flags.note: Tonight is your sixth training day in a row. Take tomorrow, Sunday July 26, completely off.
Calves are cut to two sets tonight instead of four, and the leg press does not go up. Both are deliberate, because of the six straight days.
Week 1 of a 4-week build block. Leg curls and leg extensions go up tonight; the leg press waits until after a rest day.

overrides.reason: Same as your last Legs A, on purpose. You got 220 for 8 last time and had to drop to 200 to finish, and this is your sixth straight training day — the heaviest lift on the card is the wrong place to add weight tonight.
You held 142.5 for 14 twice on Wednesday, which is the top of the range twice over. Top set goes up one pin to 150.
This day has been prescribing 120 while you were curling 135 for four straight sets on Wednesday. Matching the weight you already handle, and asking for 12 to 13 reps instead of 10.
90 gave you 15 and 14 last time, the top of the range on both sets, so the pin moves one notch to 97.5.
You got 12 reps at 127.5 last time you did this, which is the bottom of the range, so the weight stays put until you own 15 on both sets. You skipped this one last Legs A — tonight it gets done.

Two sets at 260 instead of four. Your calves did four sets on Wednesday and the last one came down from 280 to 260 to finish, and on both of your Legs A days you stopped at two sets anyway. On your sixth straight day, trim the tail of the session.
Three sets of 15 at 50 on Wednesday is every set at the top of the range — the cleanest earned step on tonight's card. 55 for 12 to 13.

dissent.progression: Open at 180 instead of 160 and hold 220 for 9 on both top sets — 220 is not his yet and the job is to own it.
dissent.recovery: Repeat July 18 exactly and add nothing: he failed to hold 220 last time, his quads worked three days ago, and this is his sixth straight training day.
dissent.why: Both seats agree 220 is the ceiling; they disagree about whether tonight is the night to consolidate it. On a sixth consecutive training day the leg press is the one lift where a bad call costs a week, and the app's own repeat would have quietly put 220 on the fourth set — the exact set he failed last time. I took the brake on the heaviest lift and spent the session's headroom on the isolation work instead, where a miss costs a set, not a block.

dissent.progression: Top set to 150 for 12 — he held 142.5 for 14 twice on Wednesday, which is the top of the range twice.
dissent.recovery: Stay at 142.5 — same muscle, same weight, only 72 hours ago, and his first set that day was 11 reps, below target.
dissent.why: Recovery is right that it was 72 hours ago and right that the opening set was short. But he then did 14 and 14 at that weight, and 150 is a single 7.5-lb pin above a load he has now handled on three consecutive leg days. This is recovering ground he already owned in December, not new territory, and a leg extension that goes badly costs one set. The brake belongs on the compound, not here.

dissent.progression: Go to 135 — the slot is stuck at 120 while he curled 135 for four straight sets on Wednesday.
dissent.recovery: Hold — his hamstrings took heavy Smith RDLs plus four sets of curls on Wednesday, and he stopped at two sets last Legs A.
dissent.why: This is the clearest case of the app under-prescribing: 120 is less than he has already proven, and on Wednesday he hit 135 for four sets with hamstrings already fatigued by RDLs. Tonight they are fresher, because nothing heavier precedes curls on Legs A. Prescribing a weight below proven work is not caution, it is a wrong number on the card — and that outranks the fatigue argument here.

dissent.progression: Four sets, 240 then 280 for 13, 13, 12 — 280 is the working weight and the ask is a rep or two more on it.
dissent.recovery: Two sets at 260 instead of four — the fourth set on Wednesday already came down from 280 to 260, and he stops at two sets on this day anyway.
dissent.why: Both seats agree the app's own plan of 280 for 15 across four sets is a number nobody earned, so that was never going to stand. Between them: progression is asking 13 reps at 280 when his best at that weight is 12, three days after doing it, at the tail end of his sixth straight day — and the program seat separately flagged that this slot dies every Legs A because it sends him back to the leg press after four other exercises. Two honest sets he will actually finish beat four he will abandon.
